questions.prompt: A session file already holds ten lines. The harness adds an eleventh line. Why does it not edit one of the old lines?
options: Editing an old line would move all the text after it, which is slower and can leave a half-written file
Editing an old line would change the version in the header
Editing an old line would hide the message from the model
Editing an old line would remove the tool result that follows it
questions.explanation: New entries go at the end, so old lines stay as they are. A crash can lose the line being written, but not the lines above it. Editing in the middle would move the rest of the file.

questions.prompt: A conversation stopped right after the user wrote Hello. The file holds a header and that message. How does the harness resume the conversation?
options: It starts a new file and copies the header into it
It sends only the last line to the model
It reads the lines, rebuilds the messages and sends them to the model in file order
It asks the user to type the earlier messages again
questions.explanation: Reading the file one line at a time gives back the message objects in the order they were written. That list becomes the history for the next request, so the conversation can continue.

questions.prompt: An agent's final reply says it ran a query on the sales table. How do you find out whether it did?
options: Read the header line for the query name
Read the log for the tool call, its arguments and the tool result
Read the system prompt for the table name
Read the final reply again for the row count
questions.explanation: The final reply is only the agent's claim. The log records each tool call and each tool result, so it shows whether the query ran and what came back.
